The source is a label, not authentication. |\\n| `caveat NAME consequence LEVEL;` | A caveat. LEVEL is `negligible`, `low`, `material`, `high` or `catastrophic`. |\\n| `CAVEAT qualifies EVIDENCE;` | The caveat goes with that evidence and everything computed from it. |\\n| `readings NAME from EVIDENCE limit N;` | A stream of up to N readings. |\\n| `decisions NAME limit N [reopened by STREAM [supporting\\\\|opposing CLAIM], …];` | A decision with up to N revisions ([triggers](reference/spec/caveat-reopening-triggers-0.1.md)). |\\n| `state NAME = EXPRESSION [min A max B];` | A number. Bounds default to, and may not exceed, `-1e12..1e12`. |\\n| `event NAME [PARAMETER, …];` | A parameter is `NAME min A max B`, `NAME in A B …`, `NAME kind KIND` or `NAME id` ([identifiers](reference/spec/caveat-identifiers-0.1.md)). |\\n| `identifiers limit N;` | Required before any `id` parameter. |\\n| `define NAME = EXPRESSION;` | A named expression, inlined where read ([define](reference/spec/caveat-define-0.1.md)). |\\n| `fn NAME(A, B) = EXPRESSION;` | A pure function. It cannot read state or evidence. |\\n| `proc NAME(PARAMETER, …) { STEP; … };` | Steps run by `call`. A parameter is a number, or `NAME readings`, `decisions`, `evidence`, `claim` or `caveat` ([procedures](reference/spec/caveat-procedure-symbols-0.1.md)). |\\n| `bind TARGET.PROPERTY = EXPRESSION [when CONDITION] [because CITATION, …];` | A displayed value. The last binding whose condition holds wins. |\\n| `clock EVENT every STEP;` | The event whose one parameter, `dt`, advances `elapsed()` ([elapsed](reference/spec/caveat-elapsed-0.1.md)). |\\n| `renewable EVIDENCE limit N;` | Evidence whose name can move to up to N distinct occurrences ([renewal](reference/spec/caveat-renewal-0.1.md)). |\\n\\n### Rules\\n\\nA rule is `on EVENT [when CONDITION] EFFECT;`. A procedure step is\\n`[when CONDITION] EFFECT;`. An event's rules run in source order, and each\\nsees what the earlier ones did.\\n\\n| Effect | Does |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `set STATE = EXPRESSION [because CITATION, …]` | Sets a number. |\\n| `sample STREAM = EXPRESSION supports\\\\|opposes CLAIM` | Records a reading. |\\n| `reveal EVIDENCE [supports\\\\|opposes CLAIM]` | Observes evidence, optionally with a stance ([neutral reveal](reference/spec/caveat-neutral-reveal-0.1.md)). |\\n| `commit SERIES because enough\\\\|budget\\\\|deadline [using EXPRESSION] [permitted by GRANT [for EXPRESSION]] [retaining CAVEAT, …]` | Makes a decision. GRANT is evidence or `latest(STREAM)`. `for X` requires the grant's value to equal X ([permission](reference/spec/caveat-permission-0.1.md)). |\\n| `reopen SERIES because EVIDENCE\\\\|latest(STREAM)\\\\|caveated(STATE, CAVEAT)` | Reopens the current revision. |\\n| `withdraw EVIDENCE\\\\|latest(STREAM) because EVIDENCE` | Marks it wrong. Later reads carry a `withdrawn` caveat ([withdrawal](reference/spec/caveat-withdrawal-0.1.md)). |\\n| `qualify EVIDENCE with CAVEAT [after SECONDS]` | Attaches a caveat now, or after that much session time. |\\n| `renew EVIDENCE` | Moves the name to a new, **unobserved** occurrence. `observed(EVIDENCE)` is false again until a `reveal`. Earlier occurrences keep what they were about. |\\n| `reject \\\"MESSAGE\\\"` | Refuses the whole event. |\\n| `call PROCEDURE(ARGUMENT, …)` | Runs a procedure's steps. |\\n\\n### Expressions\\n\\n| Kind | Forms |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Values | numbers, `true`, `false`, `\\\"text\\\"`, state and parameter names, `PARAMETER.MEMBER` for an `in` parameter |\\n| Operators | `+ - * /` (`+` also joins text), `== != < <= > >=`, `and or not` |\\n| Choice | `if(CONDITION, A, B)`, `require(CONDITION, VALUE)` |\\n| Decisions | `committed(SERIES)`, `reopened(SERIES)`, `rests_on_withdrawn(SERIES)`, `permission_withdrawn(SERIES)` |\\n| Evidence | `observed(E)`, `withdrawn(E)`, `withdrawn(latest(STREAM))`, `carries(E, CAVEAT)`, `has_caveat(STATE, CAVEAT)`, `qualified(VALUE, E[, CAVEAT…])` |\\n| Histories | `has_sample(STREAM)`, `latest(H)`, `history_count(H)`, `history_at(H, INDEX)`, `fold_history(H, INITIAL, FUNCTION)`, where H is a stream or a series |\\n| Functions | `abs min max clamp floor ceil round sqrt sin cos wrap`; text: `number_text percent_text time_text time_second_text time_total_text text id_text`; `elapsed()` |\\n\\nA value carries the evidence and caveats it was computed from, and a guard\\npasses its own to what it guards.\\n\\n## Outcomes\\n\\nAn event is **accepted**, and everything it did is kept, or **rejected**, and\\nnothing it did is kept:\\n\\n| Origin | Codes |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `policy` | `reject` (the program's own), `not_permitted` |\\n| `input` | `unknown_event`, `payload_invalid`, `bound_exceeded` |\\n| `evaluation` | `bound_exceeded` (a state outside its range), `decision_in_force` (a commit before the current decision is reopened), `ungrounded_citation` (a `because` citing what the value never read) |\\n| `limit` | `history_limit`, `identifier_limit`, `renewal_limit`, `work_limit`, `depth_limit` |\\n\\nAnything else is **fatal**, for example `require(false, …)`, arithmetic that\\nfails, or `latest` of an empty history. A fatal outcome never counts as a\\nrejection, and the session must be discarded\\n([dispatch](reference/spec/caveat-dispatch-0.1.md)). From code,\\n`session.dispatch(event, payload)` returns an accepted event's snapshot, and\\n`session.dispatchView(event, payload)` the same outcome with the view in\\nplace of the snapshot, which it does not build. In a scenario, a bare\\n`\\\"rejected\\\": true` matches any `policy` refusal. Name the code to tell the\\nprogram's own `reject` from `not_permitted`.\\n\\n## Common mistakes\\n\\nFresh agents writing programs from these documents, in the authoring trials,\\nmade the first four:\\n\\n- `--` comments. Use `#` or `//`.\\n- Bounds beyond `-1e12..1e12`, or a time counter that overflows its bounds.\\n  Read `elapsed()` instead of accumulating time.\\n- The same rules written out once per instrument. Use a `proc`;\\n  `caveat check` points these out.\\n- Lineage taken for grounds. Grounds are what `using` read; run\\n  `caveat explain` when unsure.\\n- Expecting a new reading to reconsider a decision by itself.\\n- Expecting `renew` to observe evidence. It makes a new, unobserved\\n  occurrence.\\n\\nAn agent integrating Caveat into an application made these three:\\n\\n- An event of its own named `tick`. Any `tick` may take only `dt`, within\\n  `0..0.1` seconds, even with a `clock` declaration: \\\"tick must declare only dt\\n  with bounds inside 0..0.1 seconds\\\". Name it `advance` and declare\\n  `clock advance every 1`.\\n- One parameter name listing a member at different positions in two events:\\n  \\\"origin.external_text already names a different value\\\". Each `NAME.MEMBER`\\n  is one program-wide constant. Rename one, such as to `requester_origin`.\\n- An event parameter named like a state: \\\"parameter limitations shadows state\\n  or a coordinate\\\". Rename one of them.\\n\\n## More\\n\\n- [Worked example](WORKED_EXAMPLE.md): one program through every command.\\n- [Getting started](GETTING_STARTED.md): a slower first walk through.\\n- [Authoring guide](reference/docs/AI_AUTHORING.md): time, evidence that ages,\\n  and running a session from a script.\\n- The profiles, in order: [reactive 0.1](reference/spec/caveat-reactive-0.1.md)\\n  through [0.5 histories](reference/spec/caveat-reactive-0.5.md),\\n  [0.6](reference/spec/caveat-reactive-0.6.md) and\\n  [0.7 procedures](reference/spec/caveat-reactive-0.7.md), with the\\n  [documentation index](README.md) for everything else.\\n- Not covered here: worlds and games (`place`, `entity`, `for` blocks, cues,\\n  controls), attention budgets (`budget`, `examine`, `defer`), modules and\\n  bundles.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-reactive-0.5.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT Reactive Profile 0.5 — observations and decision histories\\n\\nThis profile extends [Reactive Profile 0.4](caveat-reactive-0.4.md) with bounded\\nreading streams and decision series. Each reached sample receives its own\\nevidence identity. Each deliberate decision revision receives its own commitment\\nidentity and frozen basis. Programs can repeat an observation and revision\\nworkflow without inventing separate first, second, and third variables.\\n\\nThe runtime remains a generic Rust interpreter. These features do not introduce\\nself-hosting, arbitrary collections, historical indexing, or rule blocks. Rules\\nstill execute in source order, evaluating each rule's guard against the state\\nleft by earlier rules in the same atomic event.\\n\\n## Declaring and using histories\\n\\n```caveat\\nclaim flow_is_mild;\\nevidence forecast from \\\"morning forecast\\\";\\nevidence foam_sensor from \\\"beam-observed foam drift\\\";\\ncaveat reading_may_age consequence high;\\nforecast supports flow_is_mild;\\nreading_may_age qualifies foam_sensor;\\n\\nreadings flow from foam_sensor limit 128;\\ndecisions navigation limit 128;\\n\\nfn correction(reading) = -reading * 0.65;\\nevent start;\\nevent inspect speed min -4 max 4;\\non start commit navigation because enough using qualified(0, forecast);\\non inspect sample flow = speed opposes flow_is_mild;\\non inspect reopen navigation because latest(flow);\\non inspect commit navigation because enough using correction(latest(flow));\\n\\nbind reading.text = if(has_sample(flow), number_text(latest(flow)), \\\"Unread\\\");\\nbind command.text = if(committed(navigation), number_text(latest(navigation)), \\\"No decision\\\");\\n```\\n\\nThe syntax is:\\n\\n```text\\nreadings STREAM from EVIDENCE_TEMPLATE limit CAPACITY;\\ndecisions SERIES limit CAPACITY;\\non EVENT [when CONDITION] sample STREAM = NUMERIC_EXPRESSION supports CLAIM;\\non EVENT [when CONDITION] sample STREAM = NUMERIC_EXPRESSION opposes CLAIM;\\nlatest(HISTORY)\\nhas_sample(STREAM)\\non EVENT [when CONDITION] reopen ACTION_OR_SERIES because latest(STREAM);\\n```\\n\\nTemplates and claims must already be declared with their respective kinds.\\nHistory names cannot collide with numeric state, graph symbols, or another\\nhistory. Their generated `NAME@...` graph-symbol namespace is reserved too.\\nHistories are registered before numeric state initialization, so an initializer\\ncan use a guarded default such as `if(has_sample(flow), latest(flow), 0)`.\\n\\n## A sample is a new observation\\n\\nEvery successful `sample` effect evaluates its numeric expression and creates a\\nfresh evidence node, even when its number equals a previous sample. Names are\\ndeterministic within a session: `flow@1`, `flow@2`, and so on. The new node copies\\nthe template's canonical source string and receives the source-authored\\n`supports` or `opposes` relation to the named claim. Template qualifications are\\nlinked to the new node, and transitive qualification of its template caveats and\\nthe claim it bears on is retained. The `withdrawn` caveat of a\\n[withdrawal](caveat-withdrawal-0.1.md) is not: it is about the template's own\\nobservation.\\n\\nThe recorded value combines the expression's provenance, the sampling guard's\\nprovenance, the new occurrence's evidence identity, and its inherited caveats.\\nThe value, event sequence, source event name, identity, relation, claim, and\\nprovenance are archived together. Taking another sample does not rewrite them.\\nContrary readings can coexist in the graph with separate identities and numbers.\\n\\nCreating an occurrence does not itself mark the evidence template as observed.\\n`qualified(value, foam_sensor)` and `observed(foam_sensor)` keep their existing\\nmeanings; neither is a hidden alias for the latest reading. Evidence from an\\nunreached sample is never manufactured. Sampling does not examine a caveat,\\nspend attention, remove qualifications, or prove the sampled number is true.\\nAn application explicitly authors attention costs or time spent acquiring a\\nreading, and how that reading produces an estimate.\\n\\n`latest(flow)` returns the current archived numeric reading with its occurrence\\nprovenance and the stream's current selection dependencies. It errors before\\nthe first reached sample. `has_sample(flow)` is a boolean query for whether a\\nreading exists, allowing a lazy default without inventing a zero measurement.\\nIt accepts a reading stream, not a decision series. Both reads preserve\\nqualification tracking through functions, arithmetic, conditions, and text.\\nPure functions cannot capture a history; callers pass a `latest(...)` result as\\na numeric argument.\\n\\n## A revision is a new commitment\\n\\nThe first `commit navigation ...` creates `navigation@1`. Further commits to the\\ndeclared series require its current commitment to have been explicitly reopened.\\nA commit while it is still in force refuses the event as\\n`evaluation/decision_in_force` ([dispatch outcomes](caveat-dispatch-0.1.md));\\nnothing the event did is kept, and the session continues.\\nA successful revision creates a new commitment node, freezes its numeric\\n`using` value and provenance, and records the previous revision's identity.\\nIts inherited caveats receive `retains` edges; its evidence dependencies receive\\n`relies_on` edges. Earlier nodes, bases, retained caveats, and reopening reasons\\nremain inspectable.\\n\\n`reopen navigation because latest(flow)` resolves both the current decision and\\nthe current reading at execution time. Its graph edge names those concrete\\nidentities. The selector accepts only a reading stream. Existing\\n`reopen ACTION because NAMED_EVIDENCE` remains available. Duplicate reopening\\nedges remain idempotent; they do not invent a new observation or revision.\\n\\nFor a declared decision series, `committed(navigation)` asks whether a current\\nrevision exists, and `reopened(navigation)` asks whether that current revision is\\nopen. A new revision begins closed even though earlier revisions remain open in\\nhistory. These predicates carry the selected revision's basis and applicable\\nselection/reopening dependencies. Existing singleton commitments retain their\\nprevious behavior; repeating a singleton commit still errors.\\n\\n`latest(navigation)` returns the current revision's frozen numeric basis, plus\\ncurrent head-selection dependencies. It errors if no revision exists or its\\ncommit omitted a numeric `using` value. It does not reevaluate the expression\\nused by an earlier commitment against today's state. This lets navigation use\\nthe exact plan selected at sampling time instead of renormalizing an old sample\\nagainst a later clock value.\\n\\nAppending a revision also depends on the mandatory check that its predecessor\\nwas reopened. The new basis therefore includes that check's provenance: the old\\ndecision basis, reopening witness, and any relevant head-selection dependency.\\nThese are decision-history control dependencies. They do not claim that the new\\nmeasurement equals an older measurement or that earlier evidence is now true.\\nAn independently acquired reading can have only its own occurrence basis while\\nthe resulting decision has this broader history. The predecessor's stored basis\\nis never modified by that union.\\n\\nHistorical commitment identity, numeric basis, provenance, and predecessor links\\nare immutable. A commitment's openness may still change through an explicit\\nreopening, with the actual cause retained in the graph.\\n\\n## Selecting a current value without rewriting history\\n\\nA qualified guard can govern a decision to leave a stream or series unchanged.\\nA skipped sample or skipped series commit records that guard in a separate\\n`selection_qualifications` value. Later `latest`, `has_sample`, or current-series\\npredicates inherit it. This prevents a qualified decision to keep an older value\\nfrom silently losing its basis.\\n\\nThe archived occurrence and commitment base are not changed. A first absent\\nstream can therefore explain why no sample was taken without claiming an\\nobservation happened. An independent successful replacement clears earlier\\nselection dependencies, while qualifications actually read by its expression,\\nguard, or required predecessor check remain in the new value. Skipped reopening\\nguards use the existing predicate-dependency mechanism for the selected concrete\\ncommitment.\\n\\n## Snapshot and identity contract\\n\\nThe additive snapshot schema remains `caveat-reactive/0.1`. Existing numeric\\nvalues, qualified values, graph symbols, relations, and commitment bases remain.\\nGenerated evidence and commitment names appear in those ordinary graph fields;\\n`commitment_bases` is keyed by the concrete commitment identity.\\n\\nNew maps have these shapes:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"reading_streams\\\": {\\n    \\\"flow\\\": {\\n      \\\"template\\\": \\\"foam_sensor\\\",\\n      \\\"limit\\\": 128,\\n      \\\"current\\\": \\\"flow@1\\\",\\n      \\\"occurrences\\\": [\\n        {\\n          \\\"id\\\": \\\"flow@1\\\",\\n          \\\"ordinal\\\": 1,\\n          \\\"sequence\\\": 2,\\n          \\\"event\\\": \\\"inspect\\\",\\n          \\\"value\\\": 1.2,\\n          \\\"provenance\\\": {\\n            \\\"evidence\\\": [\\\"flow@1\\\"],\\n            \\\"caveats\\\": [\\\"reading_may_age\\\"]\\n          },\\n          \\\"relation\\\": \\\"opposes\\\",\\n          \\\"claim\\\": \\\"flow_is_mild\\\"\\n        }\\n      ],\\n      \\\"selection_qualifications\\\": {\\\"evidence\\\": [], \\\"caveats\\\": []}\\n    }\\n  },\\n  \\\"decision_series\\\": {\\n    \\\"navigation\\\": {\\n      \\\"limit\\\": 128,\\n      \\\"current\\\": \\\"navigation@2\\\",\\n      \\\"revisions\\\": [\\n        {\\\"id\\\": \\\"navigation@1\\\", \\\"previous\\\": null, \\\"ordinal\\\": 1, \\\"sequence\\\": 1, \\\"event\\\": \\\"start\\\"},\\n        {\\\"id\\\": \\\"navigation@2\\\", \\\"previous\\\": \\\"navigation@1\\\", \\\"ordinal\\\": 2, \\\"sequence\\\": 2, \\\"event\\\": \\\"inspect\\\"}\\n      ],\\n      \\\"selection_qualifications\\\": {\\\"evidence\\\": [], \\\"caveats\\\": []}\\n    }\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n`sequence` counts successful dispatched events, not wall-clock time. Applications\\nauthor their own elapsed-time values when needed. Occurrence names are local to\\nthe session and reproducible by replaying the same source and events; they are\\nnot globally unique identifiers across unrelated runs. Reading a snapshot or\\nrendering a frame cannot append a history record.\\n\\n## Bounds and failure\\n\\nEach declared capacity must be an integer in `1..256`. The sum of all reading\\nand decision capacities may not exceed 1,024. This bounds additional history\\nrecords; static graph declarations continue to use the existing profile rules.\\nThere is no eviction, silent history truncation, or published identity reuse.\\n\\nThe existing finite-number, expression, text, and per-value provenance bounds\\nremain. A long decision chain may reach its provenance bound before its declared\\nrecord capacity; that is an error rather than permission to discard its basis.\\nAny failure rejects the complete event, including samples, revisions, reopening\\nedges, numeric updates, attention spending, cues, and head-selection metadata.\\nAn aborted event consumes neither a published sequence nor an occurrence ID.\\nA `sample` or `commit` on a history that already holds its declared capacity\\nis refused as `limit/history_limit` ([dispatch outcomes](caveat-dispatch-0.1.md)),\\nand the session continues.\\n\\nThe standard library additionally provides the ordinary Caveat function\\n`wrap(value, period) = require(period > 0, value - floor(value / period) * period)`.\\nIt rejects nonpositive periods and preserves its numeric argument provenance.\\nThis brings the library to ten reserved source functions, leaving 118\\napplication functions under the existing combined 128-definition limit.\\n\\nThe non-game [thermostat history example](../examples/thermostat_history.cav)\\nuses the same sampling, reopening, and revision semantics to revise a control\\ndecision from repeated instrument readings.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-neutral-reveal-0.1.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT Neutral Reveal 0.1\\n\\nConsulting a source does not by itself support a claim. This profile adds an\\nobservation without a stance:\\n\\n```caveat\\nevidence memory from \\\"the memory lookup\\\";\\ncaveat stale consequence material;\\nevent consult;\\nevent learn_stale;\\non consult reveal memory;\\non learn_stale qualify memory with stale;\\n```\\n\\nThe evidence starts unobserved. `consult` makes `observed(memory)` true without\\ncreating a `supports` or `opposes` relation. The later qualification is valid\\nbecause the source was actually observed. No fabricated trustworthiness claim\\nis needed.\\n\\n## Syntax and meaning\\n\\n`reveal EVIDENCE` is an event-rule effect or a procedure step, including a typed\\n`evidence` procedure parameter. The existing `reveal EVIDENCE supports CLAIM`\\nand `reveal EVIDENCE opposes CLAIM` forms keep their meaning. This profile does\\nnot add neutral `sample`, neutral declaration relations, or a new decision state.\\n\\n- A successful first reveal records the current evidence occurrence as observed.\\n  It adds no claim, stance relation, reading value, or new occurrence ID.\\n- Revealing already observed evidence neutrally is a no-op. Adding a stance\\n  later adds its real relation, without changing the first-observation order.\\n  A neutral reveal after a stance also adds nothing.\\n- Observation enables the existing `qualified`, `qualify`, `withdraw`,\\n  `carries`, and explicit `reopen ... because` rules for that occurrence. It\\n  does not automatically reopen a decision or make an assessment succeed.\\n- Revealing guards and inherited procedure-call dependencies join observation\\n  lineage, not the grounds of values subsequently qualified by that evidence.\\n  Skipped guarded effects retain control dependencies using the existing\\n  `observed` predicate machinery.\\n- Declaring evidence, taking a reading from its template, and renewing it still\\n  do not observe the template/current occurrence. A renewal starts unobserved;\\n  earlier occurrences remain observed with their original identities.\\n- Late and scheduled qualification, withdrawal, frozen decision grounds and\\n  archived readings follow their existing profiles. Neutrality removes no\\n  caveats and does not change which identity a value depends on.\\n- A neutral source can be a grant only when the author explicitly names it in\\n  `permitted by E`, whose existing rule requires observed, unwithdrawn evidence.\\n  Observation itself neither grants authority nor authenticates permission.\\n- Observation is transactional: a rejected event publishes no observation,\\n  relation, provenance, binding change, or consumed ID.\\n\\nThe observation-order check recognizes both reveal forms. Uses that certainly\\nprecede any possible observation still fail at load time. A neutral reveal\\nprovides an honest on-ramp; it does not relax observed-before-qualify.\\n\\n## Snapshot, effect, and save representation\\n\\nAfter a session first records a neutral observation, snapshots and saves include\\n`observations`, an ordered list of evidence occurrence names. It contains all\\nobserved evidence, including previously observed declarations and readings,\\nexactly once in first-observation order. Subsequent samples and first stance\\nreveals append their occurrences. Renewal alone appends nothing.\\n\\nUntil a neutral observation is needed, this field is omitted and observation\\nmembership/order is derived from the existing supporting/opposing relations.\\nThus stance-only programs and their old saves retain their representation.\\nThe separate `observation_qualifications` map holds control provenance; its\\nmembership is not proof of observation, because renewal may record a guard\\nbefore the new occurrence is observed.\\n\\nA first neutral reveal reports:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"reveal\\\",\\\"evidence\\\":\\\"memory\\\"}\\n```\\n\\nA stance reveal retains `relation` and `target`. Both fields are absent for a\\nneutral reveal; exactly one present is invalid. An idempotent reveal reports\\nno new effect.\\n\\nThe save schema remains `caveat-reactive-save/0.1` with an optional observation\\nfield. New runtimes accept old saves; old runtimes need not accept saves using\\nthis extension. An explicit record must have unique known evidence names,\\ninclude every stance-observed occurrence, and preserve the initial declared\\nobservations as its prefix. Reading/renewal identities and journal/ground\\nreferences retain their existing consistency checks. Neutral-only records must\\nbe consistent with the source's possible neutral effects. Missing observation\\nproof cannot authorize otherwise unobserved evidence cited by a saved record.\\n\\nA neutral observation can precede its stance: `[B, A]` is valid for neutral B,\\nthen supporting A, then supporting B, even though the stance edges are ordered\\nA then B. Restoration must use observation order for journal evidence ordering,\\nnot reorder the ledger by when the later stance was asserted.\\n\\nThese are consistency checks on unsigned saves, not authentication of the\\nreported historical events or guards.\\n\\n## Explanations and dependents\\n\\n`explain` includes observed evidence without a stance. Its structured entry has\\n`relation: null` and `claim: null`; text says `observed (no stance)`. It includes\\ncurrent direct caveats and withdrawal status. A later real stance is shown as\\nthat relation, without an extra synthetic neutral relation. Neutral observations\\nhave no invented numeric value, event timestamp, or reading sequence.\\n\\n`dependents` follows the actual grounds and lineage, so values and decisions\\nbased on neutral evidence are discoverable like any other evidence. Neither\\nreport infers support, opposition, confidence, or external authority.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-state-caveats-0.1.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT State Caveats 0.1\\n\\nAn evidence name can be renewed while a plan still rests on its previous\\noccurrence. `carries(sighting, stale)` asks about today's occurrence. A live\\nstate that retained the plan's basis needs to ask about the evidence it\\nactually used, and name those exact occurrences when reconsidering the plan.\\n\\nThis profile exposes information the runtime already keeps. It adds no timer,\\nhistory, or saved-state table.\\n\\n## Inspecting live grounds\\n\\n```caveat\\nhas_caveat(STATE, CAVEAT)\\n```\\n\\nTrue exactly when the named numeric state's **grounds** include the named\\ncaveat. Both names are checked when the program loads. `STATE` is a declared\\nstate, not an arbitrary expression, event parameter, or evidence name.\\n\\n- Late and scheduled qualifications already update the state's grounds for\\n  each concrete occurrence it uses. Renewing an evidence alias does not change\\n  those grounds. The predicate therefore sees an older occurrence becoming\\n  stale even while a newer occurrence stays fresh.\\n- A caveat carried only by the state's control lineage does not make the\\n  answer true. A guard that happened to read stale evidence is not content.\\n- The answer's lineage is the state's full lineage, whether true or false.\\n  When read for grounds, it supplies the state's grounds. Grounded explanations\\n  can cite the answer without discarding its audit dependencies.\\n- Replacing a state's grounds reevaluates bindings that read the predicate,\\n  even when its number and the graph are unchanged.\\n- It can occur in expressions, bindings, `define`, procedure guards and state\\n  initializers reading an earlier state. Pure functions still cannot capture\\n  state. A procedure may pass the caveat through a `CAVEAT caveat` parameter;\\n  the state remains a declared name.\\n\\n## Selecting reopening witnesses\\n\\n```caveat\\nreopen ACTION because caveated(STATE, CAVEAT)\\n```\\n\\nSelect every observed evidence identity in the state's grounds that **currently\\ncarries** the caveat, directly, through another caveat, or through a claim it\\nbears on. These are concrete identities: the runtime never turns an old\\n`sighting` back into the newer `sighting@2` by resolving its renewable alias.\\nThe selection is ordered by first observation, like the decision journal.\\n\\nAn empty selection rejects the entire event without changing anything. A\\nstate may have an authored extra caveat from `qualified(value, evidence,\\nextra)` without that caveat qualifying the evidence itself. `has_caveat` can\\nthen be true while `caveated` finds no witness; the selector does not invent\\none.\\n\\nAll newly added reopening witnesses from one selector execution produce one\\n`reopened` journal entry. It records their union of caveats **now**. Individual\\nreopening graph edges and effect reports retain their existing shape. Already\\nrecorded witnesses are omitted; selecting only previously recorded witnesses\\nis idempotent and appends no entry. The state's full lineage and the selected\\nevidence's current qualifications qualify the reopening, together with the\\nusual guard and decision-selection dependencies.\\n\\nThe selector does not automatically guard against an already reopened plan.\\nThat is a policy choice, expressed as `not reopened(ACTION)`. Named evidence\\nand `latest(STREAM)` reopening selectors keep their existing behavior.\\n\\n## Example\\n\\n```caveat\\nstate plan_basis = 0;\\ndecisions plan limit 8;\\n\\non choose set plan_basis = latest_assessment;\\non choose commit plan because enough using plan_basis;\\n\\non advance when committed(plan) and not reopened(plan)\\n    and has_caveat(plan_basis, stale)\\n    reopen plan because caveated(plan_basis, stale);\\n```\\n\\nHere `latest_assessment` is a program-owned state. When its evidence ages,\\nthe separate live `plan_basis` receives the caveat even if the assessment has\\nsince changed. The commitment's original grounds and all earlier journal\\nentries stay frozen. A host reads the runtime's journal for the ordered\\nreopening causes rather than reconstructing them from unordered grounds.\\n\\nBoth operations work through module name linking and typed procedure\\nspecialization. Existing save/restore already preserves the states, exact\\nevidence identities, qualifications and journal they read. The browser bridge\\nuses the same evaluator and view; no host gameplay rule is required.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-late-qualification-0.1.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT Late Qualification 0.1\\n\\nSome caveats arrive after the fact. A taste fades from memory. An instrument\\nturns out to have been miscalibrated. A witness is discovered to have been\\nelsewhere. When that happens, everything built on that evidence should now be\\nqualified, except decisions already made: they were made on what was known\\nthen.\\n\\n```caveat\\ncaveat taste_faded consequence material;\\non tick when taste_age >= 60 qualify taste_pool with taste_faded;\\n```\\n\\nTo record that an observation is no longer stood behind, rather than add a\\ncaveat to it, see [Withdrawal 0.1](caveat-withdrawal-0.1.md).\\n\\n## Syntax\\n\\n```text\\non EVENT [when CONDITION] qualify EVIDENCE with CAVEAT;\\n[when CONDITION] qualify EVIDENCE with CAVEAT;        -- as a procedure step\\n```\\n\\n`EVIDENCE` must be declared evidence and `CAVEAT` a declared caveat. `qualify`\\nand `with` are reserved. [Renewal 0.1](caveat-renewal-0.1.md) adds\\n`qualify EVIDENCE with CAVEAT after SECONDS`, which applies the same effect\\nonce that much time has passed, to the occurrence current when it was\\nscheduled.\\n\\n## Meaning\\n\\nWhen the effect runs, `EVIDENCE` must already be observed; otherwise the event\\nfails. Then:\\n\\n1. The graph gains `CAVEAT qualifies EVIDENCE`, once. From now on every\\n   `qualified(v, EVIDENCE)` and `observed(EVIDENCE)` inherits the caveat, and\\n   any caveats that qualify it, as it would a declared qualification.\\n2. Every **current value** whose evidence includes `EVIDENCE` gains the caveat\\n   and its qualifications, in its lineage and in its grounds. The rule's guard\\n   joins the lineage only, as for any effect. Bindings are recomputed after the\\n   event, so an explanation that cites such a value shows the caveat\\n   immediately.\\n3. **What was already recorded is left alone:**\\n   - commitment bases and grounds;\\n   - the decision journal;\\n   - reading archives.\\n\\n   A decision keeps the caveats its basis carried when it was made.\\n\\nThe effect is idempotent, is reported in `effects` as\\n`{\\\"kind\\\": \\\"qualify\\\", \\\"evidence\\\", \\\"caveat\\\"}`, and is part of the event's\\ntransaction: a failed event qualifies nothing.\\n\\n## Why a language needs this\\n\\nWithout it, a late caveat has to be pushed by hand into every value that\\ncounted the evidence. Each of those values also needs a way to know whether it\\nstill counts it. In the [glowcap benchmark](https://github.com/WSattazahn/caveat-lang/blob/a24a6e91d75eeab466baa32a108ee9a242f43ac2/experiments/glowcap/RESULTS.md)\\nthat cost a plain `epoch` counter per mushroom, four fade rules per mushroom,\\nand a window test on the recovery accumulator. With `qualify`, the program\\nstates the one fact, \\\"this taste has faded\\\", and the runtime finds every value\\nthat fact touches, because provenance already records the dependency.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-withdrawal-0.1.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT Withdrawal 0.1\\n\\nEvidence can turn out to be wrong: a test log misread, a witness who was\\nelsewhere. Before this profile a program could only add a caveat to evidence\\nor record a contrary observation. In the\\n[agent ledger](https://github.com/WSattazahn/caveat-lang/blob/a24a6e91d75eeab466baa32a108ee9a242f43ac2/experiments/agent-ledger/README.md), a check result recorded\\nas passed and then found to be misread could only be followed by a failed\\none. A decision made on the misread result still cited it, with nothing to\\nmark it as wrong.\\n\\n```caveat\\nclaim misreading;\\nevidence recheck from \\\"the agent re-read the CI log\\\";\\nevent misread;\\non misread reveal recheck supports misreading;\\non misread withdraw latest(checks) because recheck;\\non misread when committed(merge) and not reopened(merge) and rests_on_withdrawn(merge)\\n    reopen merge because recheck;\\n```\\n\\nA withdrawal records that an observation is no longer stood behind, and why.\\nIt removes nothing, and it does not make the opposite claim true: withdrawing\\n\\\"the checks passed\\\" is not \\\"the checks failed\\\".\\n\\n## Syntax\\n\\n```text\\nwithdraw EVIDENCE because EVIDENCE;           -- an effect, in a rule or procedure\\nwithdraw latest(STREAM) because EVIDENCE;\\nwithdrawn(EVIDENCE)                           -- predicates\\nwithdrawn(latest(STREAM))\\nrests_on_withdrawn(DECISION)\\n```\\n\\n## What `withdraw` does\\n\\nWhen the effect runs it resolves both names to concrete occurrences:\\n- the target: named evidence resolves to its current occurrence, and\\n  `latest(STREAM)` to the stream's current reading;\\n- the reason: named evidence, resolved to its current occurrence.\\n\\nBoth must be observed, or the event fails, as `qualify` does for unobserved\\nevidence. A later renewal does not move a withdrawal to a different\\noccurrence.\\n\\nThen:\\n\\n1. **A record.** The session's `withdrawals` gains `{evidence, because,\\n   sequence, event}`. This record is authoritative: `withdrawn(E)` asks it.\\n   Withdrawing evidence that is already withdrawn keeps the first record and\\n   does nothing else.\\n2. **Current values show it.** The target gains the built-in caveat\\n   `withdrawn`, exactly as [late qualification](caveat-late-qualification-0.1.md)\\n   applies a caveat. Every current value whose lineage or grounds include the\\n   target gains it, and so does every later `qualified(…, E)` and\\n   `observed(E)`.\\n3. **Nothing recorded changes.** The observation and its relation to its\\n   claim stay. So do reading archives, every decision's frozen basis and\\n   grounds, and the decision journal. A decision keeps what it was made on.\\n\\nThe effect is part of its event's transaction, so a refused or failed event\\nwithdraws nothing. It is reported in `effects` as\\n`{\\\"kind\\\": \\\"withdraw\\\", \\\"evidence\\\", \\\"because\\\"}`.\\n\\n## Reading withdrawn history\\n\\nHistory keeps what it held: membership, order, values and recorded metadata do\\nnot change. A new computation that reads a withdrawn reading through `latest`,\\n`history_at` or `fold_history` gets that reading's value with the `withdrawn`\\ncaveat added. Copying `latest(checks)` into a state after the withdrawal gives a\\nstate that carries `withdrawn`. So reading a withdrawn value again never makes\\nit look clean, and a withdrawn reading is never skipped silently.\\n\\n## Predicates\\n\\n- `withdrawn(E)` is true when E's current occurrence is withdrawn. A fresh\\n  occurrence of renewable evidence is not withdrawn because an earlier one was.\\n  Nor is a new reading of a stream whose template is withdrawn: a `sample` is\\n  a new observation. It inherits its template's other caveats, but not\\n  `withdrawn`. A value it computes from the template, such as\\n  `qualified(v, E)`, still carries `withdrawn`, as any value read from E does.\\n- `withdrawn(latest(S))` is true when the stream's current reading is\\n  withdrawn.\\n- `rests_on_withdrawn(D)` is true when the decision's current revision was\\n  grounded on withdrawn evidence. It compares the evidence in the revision's\\n  frozen [grounds](caveat-explanations-0.2.md) against the withdrawal records:\\n  - not its frozen caveats, which record what was known then;\\n  - not its lineage, since evidence that only a guard read is not what a\\n    decision rests on.\\n\\nEach predicate carries the withdrawal's reason as its evidence. Nothing\\nreopens by itself: a program states what a withdrawal means for its decisions.\\n\\n## The built-in caveat\\n\\nA program with a `withdraw` effect has a caveat named `withdrawn`, with\\nconsequence `material`. The predicates alone do not create it: without a\\n`withdraw`, they are always false. It exists only as the effect of a\\nwithdrawal. Such a program cannot:\\n- declare anything else named `withdrawn`;\\n- apply it with `qualify`, `qualified(…)` or `commit … retaining`;\\n- `examine` it: examining does not reverse a withdrawal.\\n\\nIt may read it, as in `has_caveat(estimate, withdrawn)`.\\n\\n## Snapshot and save\\n\\nThe snapshot lists `withdrawals`, in the order they happened. A save holds the\\nsame list, and leaves it out when it is empty, so a save made before this\\nprofile restores with none. Restoring refuses a list that:\\n- names unknown evidence;\\n- gives a reason nothing observes, which `withdrawn(...)` would qualify\\n  again ([Save 0.1](caveat-save-0.1.md));\\n- withdraws evidence nothing observes, which a later `withdraw` of it would\\n  require observed again;\\n- withdraws the same evidence twice;\\n- is dated after the save's own sequence, or to an undeclared event;\\n- disagrees with the graph: every record needs its `withdrawn qualifies E`\\n  relation, and every such relation needs its record;\\n- appears in a program that does not use withdrawal.\\n\\n## Not in this profile\\n\\nThis profile does not include:\\n- undoing a withdrawal;\\n- judging whether a reason is good enough;\\n- withdrawing a reading by its value, such as \\\"the reading about commit X\\\";\\n- permission: see [Permission 0.1](caveat-permission-0.1.md), which uses\\n  withdrawal to revoke a grant.\\n\\n## Changes\\n\\n- 2026-09-27: a new reading of a stream whose template is withdrawn is not\\n  withdrawn with it. A `sample` linked every caveat qualifying its template to\\n  the new reading, `withdrawn` included, with no withdrawal record for the\\n  reading. Restore refuses a `withdrawn` relation without its record, so a\\n  session that withdrew a stream's template and then sampled the stream could\\n  not restore its own save: \\\"withdrawals disagree with the graph's withdrawn\\n  relations\\\". The reading also carried `withdrawn` into its archive, into\\n  `latest(S)` and into decisions made on it, while `withdrawn(latest(S))` and\\n  `rests_on_withdrawn(D)` stayed false. A reading now inherits its\\n  template's other caveats, declared or added later by `qualify`, as before,\\n  but not `withdrawn`, as a fresh occurrence of renewable evidence does not.\\n  Such sessions now restore; restore itself is unchanged, so a save written\\n  before this change that holds such a relation is still refused. Renewal\\n  already inherited only declared caveats, and no other effect copies a\\n  `withdrawn` relation.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-reopening-triggers-0.1.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT Reopening Triggers 0.1\\n\\nA decision often has to be reconsidered whenever a certain kind of observation\\narrives: a new push after a merge decision, a failed check after it. Before\\nthis profile, every rule that took such a reading needed its own reopening\\nrule after it:\\n\\n```caveat\\non pushed sample pushes = commit supports changed;\\non pushed when committed(merge) and not reopened(merge) reopen merge because latest(pushes);\\n```\\n\\nThe [agent ledger](https://github.com/WSattazahn/caveat-lang/blob/a24a6e91d75eeab466baa32a108ee9a242f43ac2/experiments/agent-ledger/README.md) wrote such rules by\\nhand, and forgetting one leaves a stale decision in force with nothing to show\\nit. A decision series can now declare what reopens it:\\n\\n```caveat\\ndecisions merge limit 8 reopened by pushes, checks opposing ready;\\n```\\n\\nThe program still states when the decision is reconsidered, once, where the\\ndecision is declared. The runtime carries out that statement. It does not\\njudge whether a reading is concerning enough, and it does not treat a newer\\nreading as replacing an older one, or as being about the same subject.\\n\\n## Syntax\\n\\n```text\\ndecisions NAME limit N reopened by TRIGGER, TRIGGER, …;\\nTRIGGER := STREAM | STREAM supporting CLAIM | STREAM opposing CLAIM\\n```\\n\\nEach `STREAM` must be a declared reading stream, and each `CLAIM` a declared\\nclaim. Only decision series declare triggers; a one-off commitment has no\\ndeclaration to put them on.\\n\\n## Meaning\\n\\nWhenever a `sample` records a reading into `STREAM`, and the reading's relation\\nand claim match the trigger's filter if it has one, each series with a matching\\ntrigger runs a reopening step:\\n\\n```caveat\\nwhen committed(D) and not reopened(D) reopen D because latest(STREAM);\\n```\\n\\nThe details:\\n- **When.** The step runs immediately after the reading is recorded, before\\n  the next effect, in rule order.\\n- **Guard.** It inherits the sample's guard, as a procedure step inherits its\\n  call's guard.\\n- **Semantics.** It is an ordinary reopening. Its provenance, reopening\\n  relation, journal entry, skipped-effect dependencies, execution-budget\\n  charge and rollback are exactly those of the same authored rule in that\\n  position. The decision's journal names the triggering reading.\\n- **Order.** Series are processed in name order. A series with several\\n  matching triggers runs once.\\n- **New observation, not new value.** A reading whose value repeats the last\\n  one still triggers.\\n\\nSo:\\n\\n| Sequence | Result |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| a matching reading, then the first commitment | the reading does not reopen the later commitment |\\n| a commitment, then a matching reading | the commitment reopens at once |\\n| two matching readings while one revision is in force | the first reopens it; the second finds it already open and adds nothing |\\n| a reading, a new commitment, another reading | each reading reopens the revision in force when it was taken |\\n\\nThe third row differs from an unconditional authored `reopen`, which would\\nrecord the second reading as another cause. A trigger reopens only a revision\\nstill in force.\\n\\n## What stays authored\\n\\n- Any other condition, such as \\\"and the pull request has not been merged\\n  elsewhere\\\", or a value test. The ledger keeps its own rules for exactly this\\n  reason: both of its reopening rules also require `$p_merged == 0`.\\n- Marking current values as stale.\\n- Deciding that readings are about the same subject.\\n\\n## Save\\n\\nTriggers come from the source, so saves hold nothing new. A reopening they\\ncause is recorded like any other. Restoring accepts it because the event that\\nmade it samples, directly or through a procedure, into a stream the decision\\nwatches, with a matching relation and claim. An event that could not have\\ntriggered the reopening is still refused.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-explanations-0.1.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT Explanations 0.1 — grounded citations\\n\\nA binding already carries its **lineage**: `binding_qualifications` holds every\\nevidence and caveat its value and its candidate conditions read (see\\n[Reactive 0.3](caveat-reactive-0.3.md)). Lineage is conservative on purpose.\\nNothing a presentation depended on can disappear from it.\\n\\nLineage is not an explanation. A label that says \\\"Could be a duskcap\\\" depends\\non the glowcaps that made the slime trust mushrooms *and* on the duskcap that\\nbroke that trust. The designer wants the label to cite the duskcap. Before this\\nprofile, the only way to get that was to steer lineage: order guards so `and`\\nshort-circuits before reading unrelated state, write validation to a dummy\\nstate, or override the citation in host code. The\\n[glowcap experiment](https://github.com/WSattazahn/caveat-lang/blob/a24a6e91d75eeab466baa32a108ee9a242f43ac2/experiments/glowcap/RESULTS.md) measured that cost.\\n\\nThis profile lets the author say what a binding cites, and has the runtime\\ncheck that the citation is true.\\n\\n```caveat\\nbind pool.label = \\\"Could be a duskcap — taste first\\\"\\n    when support > 0 and contradiction > 0\\n    because contradiction;\\nbind pool.label = \\\"\\\" when consumed == 1 because nothing;\\n```\\n\\n## Syntax\\n\\n```text\\nbind TARGET.PROPERTY = VALUE [when CONDITION] [because CITATIONS];\\nCITATIONS := nothing | EXPRESSION {, EXPRESSION}\\n```\\n\\n`because` is the last clause. It is recognised only outside quoted text and\\nparentheses, so `\\\"because of the rain\\\"` stays text. Each citation is an\\nordinary expression of any type; only its provenance is used. `nothing` cites\\nnothing and is reserved. A missing citation list, an empty item between commas,\\nor an unknown name is rejected before execution.\\n\\n## Meaning\\n\\nWhen a declaration supplies a shown value (the last matching one, as before),\\nits citations are evaluated against the same state. Their union is the\\nbinding's **explanation**, published per target and property in\\n`binding_explanations`.\\n\\n- **No `because` clause:** the explanation is the whole lineage. Existing\\n  programs cite exactly what they did before.\\n- **`because nothing`:** the explanation is empty.\\n- **Grounding:** every evidence and caveat in the explanation must also appear\\n  in the binding's lineage. Otherwise the event is rejected atomically:\\n  `binding pool.label cites evidence taste_cave that its value and conditions never read`.\\n  The [dispatch outcomes](caveat-dispatch-0.1.md) classify it as\\n  `evaluation/ungrounded_citation`, and the session continues. The check is\\n  made whenever a declaration supplies the shown value, so it can refuse an\\n  event long after the program loaded: a late caveat can make a declaration\\n  win for the first time on a clock tick, a renewal changes which occurrence\\n  an evidence name means, and a cited value can change apart from the shown\\n  one. A refused clock event advances no time, as with any refusal. Its due\\n  caveats do not land, so each later tick is refused the same way until\\n  another event changes what the tick would show. A declaration that already\\n  wins when the program loads is checked then, and the program does not load.\\n- **Cited values carry their caveats:** citing a value brings the caveats it\\n  carries. An explanation cannot cite evidence and drop the qualifications that\\n  travel with it. It also cannot add a qualification the binding never carried.\\n  For example, `because qualified(1, chart, manual)` is rejected if `manual`\\n  was not in the lineage.\\n- **Only the winner is evaluated.** Losing and false candidates never evaluate\\n  their citations. A binding that no declaration supplies has no explanation.\\n\\nAn explanation may therefore leave dependencies out. It may never introduce\\none. That is the honesty contract: **selective, never fabricated.** The full\\nlineage remains in `binding_qualifications` for audit. Citing less changes\\nwhat is shown to the reader, not what the runtime records.\\n\\n## What this does not claim\\n\\nThe runtime checks that a citation is *grounded*: the binding really read it.\\nIt does not check that the citation is *sufficient*, i.e. that it is the\\nreason a person would give. The author decides relevance and the runtime\\nrefuses fabrication. Explanations of commitments already exist:\\n`commitment_bases` holds a decision's frozen basis. Cues keep their existing\\n`cue_qualifications` in this profile. `caveat check` does not report a\\ncitation that can never be grounded. The runtime finds one when its\\ndeclaration first supplies the shown value, at load or long into a session.\\n\\n## Snapshot\\n\\n`binding_explanations` has the same shape as `binding_qualifications`:\\ntarget → property → `{evidence, caveats}`. It appears only for bindings that\\nare shown. The schema remains `caveat-reactive/0.1`; this is an additive field.\\n\\n## Changes\\n\\n- 2026-09-27: an event on which a citation is not grounded is refused as\\n  `evaluation/ungrounded_citation` ([dispatch outcomes](caveat-dispatch-0.1.md)),\\n  and the session continues. Before this it was a fatal `unclassified` error,\\n  so the host had to discard the session although the runtime had already\\n  rolled the event back. The check, the rollback and the diagnostic text are\\n  unchanged. The program the save tests play cites a state its label never\\n  reads, and lost its session on the tick that made that label win, 40 seconds\\n  in. It now keeps the session at 39.9 seconds and refuses every tick until a\\n  renewal replaces the bite the caveat is due on.\\n\"}\n{\"path\":\"node_modules/caveat-lang/docs/reference/spec/caveat-scenarios-0.1.md\",\"text\":\"# CAVEAT Scenarios 0.1\\n\\nA scenario file states what a reactive program should do: events to send and\\nwhat should follow. The developer kit's runner executes it through the\\n[dispatch outcome contract](caveat-dispatch-0.1.md). On every step the runner\\nalso checks what every Caveat program owes: rejected events leave nothing\\nbehind, a save resumes to the same session, and grounds stay within lineage.\\nA file states only what is specific to its program.\\n\\nThe requirements come from the\\n[coverage inventory](https://github.com/WSattazahn/caveat-lang/blob/a24a6e91d75eeab466baa32a108ee9a242f43ac2/docs/SCENARIO_COVERAGE_INVENTORY.md) of the existing\\nharnesses. Only reactive programs are in scope.\\n\\n## File\\n\\nA scenario file is UTF-8 JSON, conventionally `<program>.scenarios.json`.\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"schema\\\": \\\"caveat-scenarios/0.1\\\",\\n  \\\"source\\\": \\\"trail_rescue.cav\\\",\\n  \\\"scenarios\\\": [\\n    { \\\"id\\\": \\\"R01\\\", \\\"title\\\": \\\"…\\\", \\\"steps\\\": [] }\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n| Field | Meaning |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `schema` | Required; exactly `\\\"caveat-scenarios/0.1\\\"`. |\\n| `source` | Required; one program file, relative to this file. |\\n| `scenarios` | Required; a non-empty array. |\\n| `id` | Required; unique within the file. |\\n| `title` | Required; what the scenario shows. |\\n| `source` (scenario) | Optional; a different program for this scenario, such as a committed variant. |\\n| `steps` | Required; a non-empty array, run in order. |\\n| `note` | Optional on the file, scenarios and steps; ignored. JSON has no comments. |\\n\\nUnknown fields are errors at every level. An invalid file runs nothing.\\n\\n## Steps\\n\\nEach step has exactly one of `send`, `expect`, `same_as`, `checkpoint`,\\n`resume` or `size`, plus an optional `note`.\\n\\n### `send`\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"send\\\": \\\"read\\\", \\\"payload\\\": { \\\"value\\\": 17 } }\\n{ \\\"send\\\": \\\"advance\\\", \\\"payload\\\": { \\\"dt\\\": 0.5 }, \\\"repeat\\\": 40 }\\n{ \\\"send\\\": \\\"plan\\\", \\\"payload\\\": { \\\"target\\\": \\\"reed\\\" }, \\\"rejected\\\": \\\"Reconsider the existing plan first.\\\" }\\n{ \\\"send\\\": \\\"advance\\\", \\\"payload\\\": { \\\"dt\\\": 31 }, \\\"rejected\\\": { \\\"origin\\\": \\\"input\\\", \\\"code\\\": \\\"bound_exceeded\\\" } }\\n```\\n\\n`send` names the event. An omitted `payload` is `{}`. Any other JSON value,\\nincluding `null`, an array or a scalar, is serialized with standard JSON and\\nsent. Wrong types, missing or extra parameters and unknown members can\\ntherefore be tested. Malformed JSON text and duplicate keys cannot be written\\nin a parsed scenario file; they stay in runtime conformance tests. A payload\\nnumber that parses as non-finite, such as `1e999`, makes the file invalid,\\nbecause standard JSON would silently send it as `null`. Negative zero is sent\\nas `0`. `repeat` sends the same event 1 to 10,000 times, and every repetition\\nmust have the expected outcome.\\n\\nWithout `rejected`, the event must be accepted. Otherwise:\\n\\n| `rejected` | Matches |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `true` | A policy rejection, any message. |\\n| `\\\"<text>\\\"` | A policy rejection whose message is exactly this text. |\\n| `{\\\"origin\\\": …, \\\"code\\\"?: …, \\\"message\\\"?: …}` | That origin, and the code if given. `message` is allowed only with `\\\"origin\\\": \\\"policy\\\"`. |\\n\\nA bare expected rejection matches only `origin: \\\"policy\\\"`, so a payload\\nrefusal can never pass for a Caveat rule. `origin` is `policy`, `input`,\\n`evaluation` or `limit`. `host` is invalid in 0.1, because the runner sends\\nevents straight to the core. Codes are compared as text, so a file may name a\\ncode added after this document.\\n\\nA fatal outcome or an escaped exception never matches anything. It fails the\\nscenario and ends every session in it; the runner does not read state from a\\nsession after a fatal.\\n\\n### `expect`\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"expect\\\": {\\n    \\\"/bindings/heating/text\\\": \\\"0%\\\",\\n    \\\"/commitment_grounds/heating@2/evidence\\\": [\\\"temperature@2\\\"],\\n    \\\"/commitment_bases/heating@2/provenance/evidence\\\": [\\\"temperature@1\\\", \\\"temperature@2\\\"]\\n} }\\n```\\n\\nEach key is a JSON Pointer ([RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901))\\ninto the current snapshot. The view's fields are the snapshot's fields, except\\n`/schema`, which names each document's own schema. A pointer that works on the\\nrest of the view works here too. The snapshot adds `elapsed`,\\n`qualified_values`, `commitment_bases` and the rest of the lineage.\\n\\n- Scalars must be equal.\\n- Arrays must have the same length and match element by element, in order.\\n- Objects match partially: listed members must match, and other members are\\n  ignored. This applies at every depth.\\n- A pointer that does not exist fails, unless the expectation is `$absent`.\\n\\nA matcher is an object whose only member's name starts with `$`:\\n\\n| Matcher | Matches |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `{\\\"$exact\\\": value}` | Equal, with no extra members at any depth. |\\n| `{\\\"$set\\\": [...]}` | An array with exactly these elements in any order, counting repeats. |\\n| `{\\\"$includes\\\": [...]}` | An array that contains these elements anywhere, counting repeats. |\\n| `{\\\"$absent\\\": true}` | The pointer, or this object member, does not exist. |\\n\\nElements of `$set` and `$includes` are compared exactly, and both count\\nrepeats: `[\\\"a\\\", \\\"b\\\"]` does not match `{\\\"$set\\\": [\\\"a\\\", \\\"a\\\"]}`, and\\n`{\\\"$includes\\\": [\\\"a\\\", \\\"a\\\"]}` needs two occurrences of `\\\"a\\\"`.\\n\\nOrder is significant unless `$set` or `$includes` says otherwise. Journals, revisions and\\nreopenings are ordered; a harness that sorted every list once hid an ordering\\nbug. A literal object whose only member starts with `$` is written with\\n`$exact`. An object that mixes a matcher with other members is invalid.\\n\\n### `checkpoint` and `same_as`\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"checkpoint\\\": \\\"first\\\" }\\n{ \\\"same_as\\\": \\\"first\\\", \\\"paths\\\": [\\\"/commitment_bases/heating@1\\\", \\\"/commitment_grounds/heating@1\\\"] }\\n```\\n\\n`checkpoint` stores the current snapshot under a new name. `same_as` requires\\nthe values at `paths` to equal those in a stored snapshot exactly. Every path\\nmust exist in both snapshots; a path missing from either fails, so two absent\\nvalues never count as equal. `paths` must be a non-empty array. A whole\\nsnapshot always differs after an accepted event, because its sequence\\nadvances.\\n\\nBesides checkpoints, two names are defined:\\n\\n- `initial`: the snapshot when the session was created.\\n- `before`: the primary session's snapshot just before the most recent `send`\\n  step, before its first repetition. It exists only after the scenario's first\\n  `send` step. A file that names `before` earlier, in `same_as` or in a `size`\\n  bound, is invalid.\\n\\nA checkpoint must be defined by an earlier step of the same scenario. Its name\\nmust be new and cannot be `initial` or `before`.\\n\\n### `resume`\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"resume\\\": true }\\n```\\n\\nThe runner saves the session, restores the save text with the scenario's\\nsource, and requires an identical snapshot and view.
